title: "CP Initialization and Convergence"
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{CP Initialization and Convergence}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::knitr}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7.2,
  fig.height = 4.6,
  fig.align = "center",
  dpi = 120
)

palette <- c(
  "CP-ALS" = "#4D4D4D",
  "RGD" = "#D55E00",
  "RGN" = "#0072B2",
  "CPCA" = "#0072B2",
  "HOSVD" = "#D55E00"
)
method_lty <- c("CP-ALS" = 3, "RGD" = 2, "RGN" = 1)
method_pch <- c("CP-ALS" = 15, "RGD" = 17, "RGN" = 16)
method_pch_open <- c("CP-ALS" = 0, "RGD" = 2, "RGN" = 1)

locate_extdata <- function() {
  installed <- system.file(
    "extdata", "rebuttal_init", package = "SegreCP"
  )
  candidates <- c(
    file.path("inst", "extdata", "rebuttal_init"),
    file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "rebuttal_init"),
    installed
  )
  candidates <- candidates[nzchar(candidates)]
  found <- candidates[dir.exists(candidates)]
  if (!length(found)) {
    stop("Cannot locate the frozen rebuttal initializer-sensitivity data.")
  }
  normalizePath(found[[1L]], mustWork = TRUE)
}

read_artifact <- function(section, file) {
  utils::read.csv(
    file.path(extdata_root, section, file),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

extdata_root <- locate_extdata()

decomp_legacy <- read_artifact("decomp_ref", "trajectory_raw.csv")
decomp_legacy_init <- read_artifact(
  "decomp_ref", "initialization_summary.csv"
)
decomp_legacy_checks <- read_artifact(
  "decomp_ref", "validation_checks.csv"
)

decomp_package <- read_artifact(
  "decomp_pkg", "trajectory_raw.csv"
)
decomp_package_checks <- read_artifact(
  "decomp_pkg", "validation_checks.csv"
)
decomp_parity <- read_artifact(
  "decomp_pkg", "legacy_reference_parity.csv"
)

regression_init <- read_artifact(
  "reg_ref", "initialization_summary.csv"
)
regression_checks <- read_artifact(
  "reg_ref", "validation_checks.csv"
)

legacy_pass_col <- if ("passed" %in% names(decomp_legacy_checks)) {
  "passed"
} else {
  "pass"
}
package_pass_col <- if ("passed" %in% names(decomp_package_checks)) {
  "passed"
} else {
  "pass"
}
regression_pass_col <- if ("passed" %in% names(regression_checks)) {
  "passed"
} else {
  "pass"
}

stopifnot(
  all(decomp_legacy_checks[[legacy_pass_col]]),
  all(decomp_package_checks[[package_pass_col]]),
  all(regression_checks[[regression_pass_col]]),
  nrow(decomp_legacy) == 20L * 2L * 3L * 11L,
  nrow(decomp_package) == 20L * 2L * 3L * 11L,
  identical(sort(unique(decomp_legacy$iteration)), 0:10),
  identical(sort(unique(decomp_package$iteration)), 0:10),
  all(c("CPCA", "HOSVD") %in% decomp_legacy$initialization),
  all(c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN") %in% decomp_legacy$method)
)

mean_trajectory <- function(x) {
  aggregate(
    relative_frobenius_error ~ initialization + method + iteration,
    x,
    mean
  )
}

legacy_mean <- mean_trajectory(decomp_legacy)
package_mean <- mean_trajectory(decomp_package)

stopifnot(
  "objective" %in% names(decomp_package),
  all(is.finite(decomp_package$objective))
)
objective_raw <- decomp_package[order(
  decomp_package$replication,
  decomp_package$initialization,
  decomp_package$method,
  decomp_package$iteration
), ]
objective_key <- interaction(
  objective_raw$replication,
  objective_raw$initialization,
  objective_raw$method,
  drop = TRUE
)
objective_raw$objective_ratio <- objective_raw$objective /
  ave(objective_raw$objective, objective_key, FUN = function(z) z[[1L]])
objective_mean <- aggregate(
  objective_ratio ~ initialization + method + iteration,
  objective_raw,
  mean
)

objective_path_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(objective_raw, objective_key),
  function(z) {
    z <- z[order(z$iteration), ]
    data.frame(
      initialization = z$initialization[[1L]],
      method = z$method[[1L]],
      max_objective_increase = max(c(0, diff(z$objective)))
    )
  }
))

oracle_source <- decomp_package
oracle_key <- interaction(
  oracle_source$replication,
  oracle_source$initialization,
  oracle_source$method,
  drop = TRUE
)
oracle_path_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(oracle_source, oracle_key),
  function(z) {
    z <- z[order(z$iteration), ]
    increases <- diff(z$relative_frobenius_error)
    data.frame(
      initialization = z$initialization[[1L]],
      method = z$method[[1L]],
      path_increases = any(increases > 1e-12),
      max_oracle_increase = max(c(0, increases))
    )
  }
))

oracle_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(
    oracle_path_stats,
    interaction(
      oracle_path_stats$initialization,
      oracle_path_stats$method,
      drop = TRUE
    )
  ),
  function(z) {
    data.frame(
      Initialization = z$initialization[[1L]],
      Method = z$method[[1L]],
      Paths = nrow(z),
      `Paths with an oracle-error increase` = sum(z$path_increases),
      `Largest increase` = max(z$max_oracle_increase),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }
))
rownames(oracle_summary) <- NULL
```

This vignette turns the rebuttal-stage initialization tables into visual,
machine-checked diagnostics. It reads the frozen artifacts shipped with the
package; it does not rerun the 20-replication simulations while the package is
built. The experimental unit is one replication, and every displayed mean is
over 20 paired replications.

This vignette is evidence reconstruction, not an additional estimator API.
CP-ALS appears only as frozen experiment output. The installed package code and
`inst/scripts/ours_methods.R` implement only RGD, RGN, and initialization; the
current comparison entry point is kept outside the built package.

The scope is the CPCA-versus-HOSVD ablation newly reported in the rebuttal.
Although the historical regression run identifier came from the same
simulation workflow as an earlier figure, this vignette neither reads nor
publishes that figure's image or plotting output.

The decomposition experiment uses dimensions `60 x 30 x 30`, CP rank 3,
condition number 30, coherence 0.5, noise standard deviation 1, and 10 complete
outer sweeps. The regression rows use a `10 x 10` tensor response and a
`10 x 10 x 10` tensor predictor. Comparisons are paired within a row; values
should not be compared across the decomposition and regression tasks.

## Initialization sensitivity

The first diagnostic asks whether CPCA and HOSVD enter the refinement stage at
comparable errors. Both quantities are relative Frobenius errors: tensor error
for decomposition and coefficient error for regression. Error bars are the
frozen 95% bootstrap intervals.

```{r initialization-sensitivity, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.6, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="Initial relative Frobenius error under CPCA and HOSVD. Intervals are frozen 95% bootstrap intervals over 20 paired replications; comparisons are within rows."}
decomp_initial_plot <- data.frame(
  setting = "Decomposition (0.5, 1)",
  initialization = decomp_legacy_init$initialization,
  mean = decomp_legacy_init$initial_error_mean,
  lower = decomp_legacy_init$ci_lower,
  upper = decomp_legacy_init$ci_upper,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

regression_initial_plot <- data.frame(
  setting = sprintf(
    "Regression (%g, %g)",
    regression_init$coherence,
    regression_init$noise_sd
  ),
  initialization = regression_init$initialization,
  mean = regression_init$initial_error_mean,
  lower = regression_init$initial_error_lower,
  upper = regression_init$initial_error_upper,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

initial_plot <- rbind(decomp_initial_plot, regression_initial_plot)
setting_order <- c(
  "Decomposition (0.5, 1)",
  "Regression (0, 0.5)",
  "Regression (0, 1)",
  "Regression (0.5, 0.5)",
  "Regression (0.5, 1)"
)
initial_plot$y <- match(initial_plot$setting, rev(setting_order))

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mar = c(4.2, 8.2, 2.6, 0.8), las = 1)
plot(
  range(initial_plot$lower, initial_plot$upper),
  range(initial_plot$y) + c(-0.45, 0.45),
  type = "n",
  axes = FALSE,
  xlab = "Initial relative Frobenius error",
  ylab = "",
  main = "CPCA and HOSVD initialization error"
)
axis(1, col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
axis(
  2,
  at = seq_along(setting_order),
  labels = rev(setting_order),
  tick = FALSE,
  cex.axis = 0.86
)
abline(h = seq_along(setting_order), col = "#ECECEC", lwd = 1)
for (initializer in c("CPCA", "HOSVD")) {
  z <- initial_plot[initial_plot$initialization == initializer, ]
  offset <- if (initializer == "CPCA") 0.09 else -0.09
  segments(
    z$lower, z$y + offset, z$upper, z$y + offset,
    col = palette[[initializer]], lwd = 2
  )
  points(
    z$mean, z$y + offset,
    col = palette[[initializer]],
    pch = if (initializer == "CPCA") 16 else 17,
    cex = 1.05
  )
}
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("CPCA", "HOSVD"),
  col = palette[c("CPCA", "HOSVD")],
  pch = c(16, 17),
  bty = "n",
  horiz = TRUE,
  inset = c(0, -0.01)
)
box(bty = "l", col = "#666666")
par(old_par)
```

CPCA has the lower mean initial error in every displayed setting. This is an
initialization comparison, not evidence that one optimizer must have the best
terminal error.

## Full decomposition trajectories

The next figure overlays the rebuttal-stage trajectory (solid lines and filled
points) and the package compatibility rerun (dashed lines and open points).
Color, line type, and point shape jointly identify the methods and sources.

```{r decomposition-trajectories, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.6, fig.height=4.4, fig.cap="Mean decomposition error over all 10 sweeps. Solid filled trajectories are the rebuttal-stage results; dashed open trajectories are the package compatibility rerun."}
trajectory_ylim <- range(
  legacy_mean$relative_frobenius_error,
  package_mean$relative_frobenius_error
)
trajectory_ylim <- trajectory_ylim + c(-0.02, 0.02) * diff(trajectory_ylim)

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(
  mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.7, 3.0, 0.8),
  oma = c(0, 0, 1.0, 0), las = 1
)
for (initializer in c("CPCA", "HOSVD")) {
  plot(
    0:10,
    rep(NA_real_, 11),
    type = "n",
    ylim = trajectory_ylim,
    xlab = "Completed outer sweeps",
    ylab = "Mean relative tensor error",
    main = paste(initializer, "initialization"),
    axes = FALSE
  )
  axis(1, at = seq(0, 10, by = 2), col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
  axis(2, col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
  abline(h = pretty(trajectory_ylim), col = "#ECECEC", lwd = 1)
  box(bty = "l", col = "#666666")

  for (method in c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")) {
    z_legacy <- legacy_mean[
      legacy_mean$initialization == initializer &
        legacy_mean$method == method,
    ]
    z_package <- package_mean[
      package_mean$initialization == initializer &
        package_mean$method == method,
    ]
    z_legacy <- z_legacy[order(z_legacy$iteration), ]
    z_package <- z_package[order(z_package$iteration), ]

    lines(
      z_legacy$iteration,
      z_legacy$relative_frobenius_error,
      col = palette[[method]],
      lty = 1,
      lwd = 2.1
    )
    points(
      z_legacy$iteration,
      z_legacy$relative_frobenius_error,
      col = palette[[method]],
      pch = method_pch[[method]],
      cex = 0.68
    )
    lines(
      z_package$iteration,
      z_package$relative_frobenius_error,
      col = palette[[method]],
      lty = 2,
      lwd = 1.6
    )
    points(
      z_package$iteration,
      z_package$relative_frobenius_error,
      col = palette[[method]],
      pch = method_pch_open[[method]],
      cex = 0.72
    )
  }

  if (initializer == "CPCA") {
    legend(
      "topright",
      legend = c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN"),
      col = palette[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      pch = method_pch[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      lty = rep(1, 3),
      lwd = 1.8,
      bty = "n",
      cex = 0.80
    )
  } else {
    legend(
      "topright",
      legend = c("Rebuttal-stage legacy", "Package rerun"),
      col = "#333333",
      pch = c(16, 1),
      lty = c(1, 2),
      lwd = c(2.1, 1.6),
      bty = "n",
      cex = 0.80
    )
  }
}
mtext("Rebuttal-stage and package decomposition trajectories", outer = TRUE)
par(old_par)
```

The CPCA trajectories agree to numerical precision. The archived HOSVD package rerun is
deliberately **not** labeled an exact legacy replay: `SegreCP` stores a
canonical representation with nonnegative component weights, whereas the
historical HOSVD route used a sign-dependent component ordering. The frozen
parity audit therefore checks mean-path and checkpoint tolerances as well as
method ranking, instead of requiring identical HOSVD iterates.

```{r parity-summary, echo=FALSE}
parity_display <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Maximum CPCA trajectory difference",
    "Maximum CP-ALS trajectory difference",
    "Maximum mean-trajectory difference",
    "Maximum 3/5/10 checkpoint difference",
    "Checkpoint method ranking preserved",
    "CPCA/HOSVD contrast preserved"
  ),
  Value = c(
    format(decomp_parity$cpca_max_absolute_difference, scientific = TRUE),
    format(decomp_parity$cpals_max_absolute_difference, scientific = TRUE),
    format(
      decomp_parity$max_absolute_mean_trajectory_difference,
      scientific = TRUE
    ),
    format(
      decomp_parity$max_absolute_checkpoint_difference,
      scientific = TRUE
    ),
    as.character(decomp_parity$method_ranking_preserved),
    as.character(decomp_parity$initializer_contrast_preserved)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(parity_display, row.names = FALSE)
```

These checks establish reproducibility of the reported pattern under the
package's canonical representation. They do not turn an empirical trajectory
comparison into a proof of global convergence.

## Objective convergence in the archived package rerun

For CP-ALS, RGD, and RGN, the archived package artifact records the same observed
least-squares objective at every completed sweep. The figure normalizes each
replication by its iteration-0 objective and then averages the ratios. The
vertical scale is focused on the observed range; it does not start at zero.

```{r objective-convergence, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.4, fig.height=4.1, fig.cap="Mean observed-objective ratio for the 20 package reruns. The vertical axis is focused on the observed range and does not begin at zero."}
objective_ylim <- range(objective_mean$objective_ratio)
objective_ylim <- c(
  floor(100 * objective_ylim[[1L]]) / 100,
  min(1.005, objective_ylim[[2L]] + 0.005)
)

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(
  mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.8, 3.0, 0.8),
  oma = c(0, 0, 1.0, 0), las = 1
)
for (initializer in c("CPCA", "HOSVD")) {
  plot(
    0:10,
    rep(NA_real_, 11),
    type = "n",
    ylim = objective_ylim,
    xlab = "Completed outer sweeps",
    ylab = "Mean objective / initial objective",
    main = paste(initializer, "initialization"),
    axes = FALSE
  )
  axis(1, at = seq(0, 10, by = 2), col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
  axis(2, col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
  abline(h = pretty(objective_ylim), col = "#ECECEC", lwd = 1)
  box(bty = "l", col = "#666666")

  for (method in c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")) {
    z <- objective_mean[
      objective_mean$initialization == initializer &
        objective_mean$method == method,
    ]
    z <- z[order(z$iteration), ]
    lines(
      z$iteration,
      z$objective_ratio,
      col = palette[[method]],
      lty = method_lty[[method]],
      lwd = 2
    )
    points(
      z$iteration,
      z$objective_ratio,
      col = palette[[method]],
      pch = method_pch[[method]],
      cex = 0.72
    )
  }
  if (initializer == "CPCA") {
    legend(
      "topright",
      legend = c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN"),
      col = palette[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      lty = method_lty[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      pch = method_pch[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      lwd = 2,
      bty = "n",
      cex = 0.82
    )
  }
}
mtext("Observed objective convergence (focused vertical scale)", outer = TRUE)
par(old_par)
```

```{r objective-check, echo=FALSE}
objective_check <- data.frame(
  Recorded.paths = nrow(objective_path_stats),
  Paths.with.an.increase = sum(
    objective_path_stats$max_objective_increase > 1e-10
  ),
  Largest.increase = max(objective_path_stats$max_objective_increase),
  check.names = FALSE
)
names(objective_check) <- c(
  "Recorded paths", "Paths with an increase", "Largest increase"
)
knitr::kable(objective_check, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
```

## Oracle error and the noise floor

The relative error to the simulated truth is scientifically useful, but it is
not the objective minimized by the algorithms. Consequently, an individual
oracle-error path may rise slightly after reaching the statistical noise floor
even while the observed objective continues to decrease.

```{r oracle-floor-summary, echo=FALSE}
oracle_display <- oracle_summary
oracle_display[["Largest increase"]] <- format(
  oracle_display[["Largest increase"]],
  scientific = TRUE,
  digits = 3
)
knitr::kable(oracle_display, row.names = FALSE)
```

This distinction is why the full trajectories are reported as empirical
convergence diagnostics rather than as evidence of global convergence or
per-replication monotonicity of the unknown-truth error.
